generator: tools/name-vectors.mjs via tools/release.mjs (viem keccak256; the grammar from the NatSpec of src/profiles/FilesNameRule.sol)

grammar.name: 1..255 bytes of strict UTF-8, byte-exact and case-sensitive (nothing normalized); no C0 control, DEL or C1 control; none of the ASCII in `asciiRefused`; none of the excluded scalars (U+2028-2029, bidi controls, pure invisibles, U+FFF9-FFFD, noncharacters); no Unicode whitespace first or last; not starting with `~efs`; not ending with '.' (so not '.' or '..')
rulings: James, 2026-11-26: "? # etc shouldn't be allowed as they are literally urlencode protected params. Nothing that breaks URLs. Nothing that breaks OS file paths."
James, 2026-11-26, later the same day (withdraws the OS-path test): "Don't refuse windows reserved names. I only care about URI safety and us having some delimiters we can use for URL syntax"

asciiRefusedBecause.note: URI meaning: each changes what a pasted link means ('/' and '\' since files-name/2). Delimiter kept free: reserved for EFS URL syntax, which is not designed (only the reservations are made); ';' is reserved so a parser can split parameters at ';' first, which is why '=' and '!' stay admitted

grammar.trailingDot: refused for link trimming (chat apps and auto-linkers trim a full stop after a pasted link, so /docs/inc. would open /docs/inc): the integration owner's application, not James's ruling, and a check of its own; it also refuses '.' and '..', as files-name/2 did
grammar.admitted: spaces inside a name, & ( ) ' , + = ! @ $ [ ] { } ^ ~ ` - _, leading dots and a leading '-'; ZWJ/ZWNJ, variation selectors and tag characters; Windows device names (CON, nul.txt) are ordinary names

reasons.ascii: a C0 control, DEL or a character of asciiRefused
reasons.excluded: a C1 control or another excluded scalar

grammar.reasonNote: informative: the chain answers one refusal (E_FILES_REFUSED(2)); `reason` is the first failed check in the order FilesName.valid runs them (length, reserved-prefix, the scan in byte order, trailing-dot, whitespace)
grammar.error: E_FILES_REFUSED(uint8 code) on a direct call; through the kernel E_REJECTED(leaf, typeId)
grammar.sdk: refuse before building a plan; NFC and any case policy are the SDK's, the chain never normalizes
grammar.open: Q7: two names that differ only by capitals or by Unicode normalization (Report.txt and report.txt) are two distinct names on chain (byte-exact); whether that stays so is open before any lasting deployment
